concepts.title: Ardha-Kukkuṭī-Nyāya — The Half-Hen Fallacy
concepts.excerpt: A man buys a hen. He wants the eggs but resents the feeding, so he proposes a division: he will keep the half that lays and dispose of the half that eats.

concepts.title: Arthavāda — Reading Scripture for Intent, Not Narrative
concepts.excerpt: There is a grammarian's example the compendium reaches for when it wants to make a point about reading, and it is a good one because it is annoying.

concepts.title: Three Births, Three Kalpas — Plurality Without Adjudication
concepts.excerpt: Ask a tradition where its central figure came from and you expect one story, possibly with variants at the edges.

concepts.title: The Three Darśanas Simultaneously True: Hanumān's Secret Teaching
concepts.excerpt: Picture Hanumān kneeling in front of Rāma. Ask him who he is and you get three different answers, and he means all of them at the same time.

concepts.title: Swallowing the Sun as Siddhi, Not Hyperbole
concepts.excerpt: An infant wakes hungry, sees something round and red in the sky, and goes for it.

concepts.title: The Maṅgala Paradox — Ill Omen and Embodied Auspiciousness
concepts.excerpt: There is a line in which the figure himself gives the warning: hear my name first thing in the morning and you will go without food that day.

concepts.title: The Twelve Names of Hanuman
concepts.excerpt: There is a kind of text that is not meant to be read so much as carried.

concepts.title: Hanumān: Patron God of the Akhara
concepts.excerpt: In every akhara, one red figure looks out over the pit, and even Muslim wrestlers show him respect.

concepts.title: Confirmation Bias as Ancient Problem — The Sickle-Thief and 2,500 Years Before Kahneman
concepts.excerpt: A man loses his ax. He suspects his neighbor stole it. He watches his neighbor walk, and it looks like the walk of a man who stole an ax.

concepts.title: Selective Honesty as Control Mechanism
concepts.excerpt: A man walks into Al Capone's office in 1926 and asks for fifty thousand dollars.
